aoj_help_start_text: Found a settlement Build a Jarl's Table (hammer, no workbench needed). It founds a settlement around itself: a radius of 30 m, growing with the tier and with every member (up to 60 m). Two tables need 150 m between them. Tiers 0-7 come from the bosses you have beaten in this world: a higher tier allows more settlers, more jobs, more combat roles and bigger totems. The table's window [E]: Settlement (name, tier, alarm), Members (ranks), Settlers (accept, orders, dismiss), Work (totems, hand assignment), Storage (what the chests hold), Defence (banners, breaches), Chronicle (who did what). First steps 1. The table. 2. A few beds, public chests and a Settlement Cauldron with food inside the radius. 3. Recruit settlers (next chapter) and accept them at the table. 4. Plant a Work Totem, put an axe or a pickaxe into a chest, and watch.
aoj_help_settlers_text: Who they are Every settler has a name, looks, an origin and up to three of 13 traits (Diligent, Strong, Hawk-eyed, Night Owl, Veteran, Cowardly...) that change its pace, strength, courage or appetite. Hover over a settler to see what it is doing right now. Recruiting - Castaways reach the shore once your first table stands: talk to them [E]. - Captives wait behind bars in enemy camps (in old worlds too): beat the guards or break the bars and free the captive [E]; it follows you. Take it home and accept it at the table (Settlers tab) - it gets a bed and lives there. - A follower whose own table was destroyed can be accepted at another table. The settler's window [E] Traits and needs, its combat role and its job, and the Equipment tab: Take / Take 1 puts an item back into your bag, Take everything back the whole bag - in co-op too, whichever machine simulates it. Give it something by using the item on it: food is eaten on the spot; weapons, tools and armour go into its bag. Hurt and death A settler whose health runs out is knocked out, not killed (Settlers/PermanentDeath changes that): nobody attacks it, it keeps its gear and gets up after a while. A badly wounded settler goes to bed to heal.
aoj_help_orders_text: Command wheel [{wheel}] (Commands/WheelKey) Looking at a settler (up to 40 m): Come to me, Stay, Attack (what you look at), Fall back, Go home, Details (its window). Looking elsewhere: the same orders for your whole squad - everyone who follows you - with the creature in your sight as the target. The game's own wheel [G] has the squad orders under Commands. 'Follow me' also reaches settlers up to 20 m away that follow nobody. Guards A settler that follows you is your guard. It walks at your shoulder - several walk in pairs behind you - and stays out of your camera. It fights the enemies that come for you (Commands/GuardRange, 15 m), the one going for you first, and never chases farther than Commands/GuardLeash (30 m) from you. It comes with you through portals and steps aside when you walk into it. Your orders win: an attack order holds for 30 s, a fall-back for 8 s, over anything a settler would do on its own. Home: 'Go home' sends a settler back to its settlement; a settler with no home waits where it stands.
aoj_help_work_text: Work Totems Standards you plant anywhere in the settlement (hammer, no workbench): Woodcutter, Hauler, Miner, Smelter, Builder, Farmer, Cook. Each totem has a zone (8-30 m), working hours (day or all day) and a priority. Free settlers take free places by themselves, the highest priority first - or you assign by hand (table, Work tab). Upgrade a totem (3 levels) for more places and faster work; more members give more places too. Tools come from you: put axes, pickaxes and hammers into the settlement's chests and a worker fetches what it needs. - Woodcutter: trees, logs, stumps, replanting. - Miner: rocks and ore veins. - Hauler: loose items in its zone and the input chest (a public chest within 4 m of its totem): dump anything into it and it gets sorted into the chests. - Smelter: ore and fuel into smelters and kilns, bars out. - Cook: raw food onto cooking stations, meals into the cauldron. - Farmer: planting and harvest. - Builder: puts back what sieges destroyed. Idle hands help: a worker whose own totem has nothing for it lends a hand at another totem of the settlement after a while, and comes back when its own work returns. Carrying: a worker takes its load to the chests when its bag is nearly full (Work/CarryLimit) or its work is done; the Strong carry more; a part load waits a moment for more work. While you are away (up to 2 days): on your return the settlement credits the work it would have done - wood, stone, bars, cooked food, harvest - from what the chests held.
aoj_help_storage_text: Sorted chests Settlers put things into the settlement's public chests by rule: where the same item already lies, then where its kind lies (wood with wood, hides with hides), then into an empty chest - never mixing kinds in one chest. The chest that takes the most of a load is the one walked to. A chest's kind: [Shift+E] on a chest cycles wood, ore, food... ('any' = sorted as usual). Such a chest takes that kind only, before any other chest. Settlement Cauldron: food goes there first; settlers eat from it. Keep it stocked - Cooks do. Left alone by settlers: private chests, carts and ships, the Obliterator, the Armory (the troop's), and a Hauler's input chest (emptied, never filled). Warehouses: an area marked on the map as a warehouse (chapter Map) is part of the settlement - its chests are filled and emptied like the ones at home, also behind a portal. Storage tab of the table: every chest and the totals. 'No chest takes it': a settler carrying something no chest accepts says so when you hover over it - build a chest or give one a kind.
aoj_help_needs_text: Hunger Satiety (0-100) falls with time (Needs/SatietyPerDay). Below Needs/HungryBelow (45) a settler is hungry: it eats from its bag, else at the nearest Settlement Cauldron with food, else fetches food from a chest (and some for the cauldron), picks up food lying around, and as a last resort forages berries and mushrooms. Close to hungry it has a bite between two tasks. A starving settler works at half pace. Morale (0-100) comes from satiety, a bed, variety of meals, traits and feasts; it sets the work pace (x0.6 to x1.25). Miserable settlers may refuse to work (Needs/RefuseWorkWhenMiserable). Beds: a free bed inside the settlement is given to a settler by itself; it sleeps there at night and heals faster there. Build enough beds. Wounds: below 40% health a settler goes to bed. By day a worker gets up again at 75% and finishes healing on its feet; at night, or without a job, it stays until well. A settlement that unlocked healers heals twice as fast in bed. Sleep: at night settlers finish their trip, store their load, eat if hungry and go to bed. Night Owls work on.
aoj_help_army_text: Roles (settler window): Warrior, Archer, Shieldbearer, Spearman (tier 4), Berserker (tier 5). A soldier takes the gear of its role from the Armory (a piece: put weapons, shields, bows, arrows and armour in it) and brings worn-out gear back for you to repair. A soldier with a job mans its post only during an alarm. War Banners: Rally (any soldier), Wall (archers), Gate (shieldbearers hold the breach), Shelter (civilians hide there during an alarm). Soldiers without a job stand at their post by day. How they fight: they block a blow about to land (perfectly once they know the creature), turn on the one striking them, fight with the weapon of their role; archers keep their distance and kite in bursts; the troop focuses fire on the enemy its comrades fight, the most wounded first; nobody shoots through a comrade. Alarm: sounds by itself when enough alerted enemies stay inside the settlement for a few seconds (Sieges/AlarmMinThreats), or by hand at the table. Civilians hide, soldiers man their posts, everyone gets a message and a map pin. It ends when it has been quiet for a while. Sieges: from tier 1 the settlement is sometimes besieged while you are home (Sieges/IntervalDays, Chance, Strength); more players at home, bigger sieges. Builders put back what was destroyed; the Defence tab lists the breaches.
aoj_help_map_text: Settlers loaded around you are on the map and the minimap like players, in gold (UI/SettlerPins, UI/SettlerPinColor). The map's player filter hides them too. Settlers beyond the loaded zones are not shown: nothing on your machine knows where they are. Settlement: a circle of its radius around the table (UI/SettlementAreas). Areas [{zone}] on the big map (Commands/ZoneKey): press it over a spot to mark an area of the nearest loaded settlement you may manage (Hersir and up) - a warehouse (its chests count as the settlement's) or any other named area. Press it over an existing area to edit or remove it. Up to 16 areas, within 400 m of the table, radius 5-80 m; warehouses are blue, other areas green. Alarm pins appear on everyone's map while an alarm is on.
aoj_help_portals_text: Your jump is quicker: half a second in the dark instead of two (Portals/PlayerTeleportSeconds), and at most two seconds for the far side to load instead of six (Portals/DistantLoadSeconds). Followers come along: settlers following you within 20 m are at the other side when you step out (Settlers/FollowThroughPortals). Knocked-out and captive ones stay. Settlers use portals (Portals/SettlerPortals): every trip - to a chest, a tree, a station, a bed, home from afar - goes through a portal within 80 m when the far end lands much closer to the goal, and back the same way. A settler left far from home takes a portal home when one leads there. Mind the game: settlers only act where the world is loaded, around players. A settler that jumped into an unloaded area appears when somebody gets there.
aoj_help_coop_text: Everyone needs the mod, the server too, in the same version (the mod updates itself - chapter About). Ranks (table, Members tab): up to two Jarls with equal rights; Hersirs run the settlement (areas, totems, lower ranks); Huscarls lead the troop (roles, banners, alarm); Karls live there and bring and order their own settlers; guests only look. The founder is the first Jarl and can hand the title on. Bigger together: every member adds the tier's settler limit again, more radius and more places at the totems (Settlement/MemberBonus, MemberRadiusBonus). Sieges grow with the number of players at home. Who simulates a settler is whichever machine is nearest; orders, items and portal jumps reach it wherever it is simulated. Taking items from a settler works from every machine; what you take arrives in your bag or at your feet.
aoj_help_keys_text:
[E] talk to a settler; open the table, a totem, a banner, the Armory
[Shift+E] on a chest: its kind
[{wheel}] command wheel (Commands/WheelKey)
[G] the game's wheel - group Commands
[{zone}] on the big map: areas (Commands/ZoneKey)
[{help}] this manual (UI/HelpKey)
[Esc] closes the mod's windows

Use an item on a settler to give it (food is eaten at once). In a settler's window: Take / Take 1 / Take everything back.

The mod's windows scale with UI/Scale.
aoj_help_console_text:
Console [F5], 'devcommands' first.

aoj_info - settlement, totems and settlers around you
aoj_settlers, aoj_settlement - lists
aoj_debug - what each settler is doing, over its head
aoj_trace - the settlers' decisions in the log
aoj_perf [seconds] - performance report
aoj_spawn [name], aoj_despawn [radius] - test settlers
aoj_give <item> [count] [name] - hand gear to a settler
aoj_role <role> [name], aoj_rank <rank> <player>, aoj_jarl <player>, aoj_rename
aoj_totem assign|radius|priority|upgrade, aoj_place <piece>, aoj_fill <item> [count]
aoj_tier <0-7> - the settlement's tier, for testing
aoj_catchup <hours> - credit the work of an absence now
aoj_siege, aoj_alarm on|off, aoj_breach [damage], aoj_captive, aoj_morale <0-100>
aoj_defs, aoj_reload_defs, aoj_dump <prefab>, aoj_version
aoj_help_settings_text: Configuration: BepInEx/config/{config} (Configuration Manager: F1). Synced from the server where marked. Settlers: BaseHealth, PermanentDeath, FleeHealthThreshold, Blocking, CollectLoot, LootRange, FollowThroughPortals, FriendlyFire, CollideWithPlayers and CollideWithSettlers (off: you and they walk through each other - no more being shoved in a doorway; hits land either way). Commands: WheelKey, LookRange, FollowMeRange, GuardRange, GuardLeash, ZoneKey. Work: WorkSpeed, CarryLimit, TotemBaseSlots, TotemMaxSlots, TotemReach. Needs: SatietyPerDay, HungryBelow, RefuseWorkWhenMiserable. Settlement: MinDistance, MaxJarls, MemberBonus, MemberRadiusBonus. Sieges: Enabled, IntervalDays, Chance, Strength, PerPlayer, AlarmMinThreats, AlarmCooldownSeconds. Recruitment: CaptiveCampChance, Castaways. CatchUp: MaxDays. Portals, UI, Updates: see those chapters. UI/HelpKey: this manual. Balance data in BepInEx/config/AgeOfJarls/*.json: traits, tiers, names, storage kinds, siege waves, totem levels (aoj_reload_defs reloads them).
aoj_help_about_text: Age of Jarls {version} In the main menu the mod looks at its update page (Updates/Url), downloads a newer version, checks it and puts it in place for the next start of the game; a message in the game tells you when a restart is due. Off with Updates/AutoUpdate. Everyone on a server stays on the same version this way. The changelog lies next to the mod (CHANGELOG.md). When something looks wrong: aoj_debug shows what a settler is doing, aoj_trace writes its decisions to BepInEx/LogOutput.log.
